newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zedillo unveils 1997 jobs program.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo unveils 1997 jobs program.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo unveiled a jobs program for 1997 that aims to create up to one million temporary jobs in a country where many desperately need work.

Zedillo said his government would spend 2.15 billion pesos this year alone through several government agencies, especially those involved in agriculture and public works. He said a similar program in 1995 and 1996 had created 1.5 million jobs.

The president said recent news the economy grew 5.1 percent in 1996 showed that the country now "sees the light at the end of the tunnel" following the nation's most serious recession in more than a half century.
Zedillo's long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) hopes more jobs can ease widespread anger about the crisis and help the PRI survive key mid-term elections in July.
He said the millions of jobs lost during the crisis were what hurt him most about the crisis, started in late 1994 with a surprise devaluation of the peso by Zedillo.
